rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed Oct 28 hold ~91–93%, Dec hike >80%; BoC Oct 28 hike ~75–80% (TD, Rabobank: hold); RBNZ Oct 28 hike ~85–89%; ECB Oct 29 hold ~93–97%; BoJ Oct 30 hold ~98%; RBA Nov 3 ~50%; BoE Nov 5 hike ~94%
rows.read: Five central banks decide this week, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Canada and New Zealand are expected to hike; the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan are expected to hold. Falling oil makes the case for more hikes a little weaker everywhere.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Chicago Fed activity index Sep +0.07 (−0.10 fc); Germany Ifo Oct 90.2 (90.0 fc), expectations 91.6; UK CBI retail sales Oct −10 (−47 fc)
rows.read: Monday's surveys were better than feared. German firms are more hopeful about the months ahead, UK retailers saw sales fall far less than expected, and US activity ran slightly above its normal pace. None of it moved currencies much before a week full of central-bank decisions.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent ~$110 (from ~$117 Fri); US 1-yr inflation expectations 4.7% (Michigan, Oct final); Japan core CPI Sep 2.1%; UK CPI Sep 3.5%; Australia Q3 CPI Tue 7:30 PM CT
rows.read: Energy is still the main reason inflation runs above target in most big economies. Monday's drop in oil helps a little, but central banks will want to see it last. Australia's inflation figures on Tuesday evening, CT, are the week's first big test of that.

rows.title: Risk
rows.figure: US stock futures higher (Oct 26); US 10Y ~4.97%; USD/JPY ~157.1 (+0.2%); gold ~$4,008
rows.read: Markets calmed as diplomats went to Tehran and the weekend passed without new US strikes. That cut demand for safe places to park money, so the yen eased a little. Fresh attacks or failed talks would quickly reverse that.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$110 (about −6% from Fri); WTI ~$101.08 (from $103.27); Houthi claim on Saudi East-West pipeline unconfirmed
rows.read: Oil fell sharply as regional envoys pressed Iran to avoid new fighting. That helps big energy importers like Japan and the euro area and takes some support away from Canada. The drop has not yet moved those currencies much.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD (sharply added) and EUR (added), for GBP (real money strongly against), for AUD (real money strongly against), leaning against JPY (flipped), strongly for gold (trimmed)
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Moody's held France at Aa3, negative outlook (Oct 23); French revenue-section vote Tue Oct 27; UK Budget Wed Oct 28 ~7:30 AM CT
rows.read: Pressure on France eased after Moody's held its rating, which helped the euro early on Monday. Britain's first Budget from Chancellor Healey on Wednesday is now the bigger test: heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound.
